study: Repeated policy queries with checked dual reuse and persistent LP baselines
status_at_registration: planned before any timed workload result

query_engine.scope: Controlled execution programs with known feasible witnesses, not sampled confidence sets or empirical coverage trials. Include the common view construction and plan/checker initialization in cumulative query totals.
query_engine.hypothesis: Prepared checked reuse takes at most 80% of persistent HiGHS basis-hot-start time including common view construction, initialization, query execution, proof creation and serialization, with no invalid proof. Report all repeats and median paired ratio; no p-value with only three timing repeats.
query_engine.support_rule: The timing target is supported only if all three primary paired time ratios are <=0.8; no timing-result-based configuration filtering.

end_to_end.scope: Actual encoded event columns read from .npy files, validated and counted; source intervals, feasible witness, plan/checker initialization, queries and proof serialization timed. Event generation and saved audit replay are outside serving latency and reported separately. No claim about SQL engine performance or cold disk I/O.

query_definition: Uniform reference; nearby queries independently perturb both within-block contrast directions, not only their scale. Unrelated queries are centered normal vectors rescaled so every policy probability remains >=0.2/d. First query, all cache misses, and all unresolved outputs retained.
comparison: All methods receive exactly the same represented view and ordered query objectives and use the same exact arithmetic acceptance rule. A cache bound can be looser; compare decisions and bound differences separately. Full-alpha/source-statistical comparisons belong to separate studies.
timing: Pin the entire timed process to the first CPU in its inherited allowed affinity, single native solver thread and BLAS=1; randomize method order within each paired repeat using fixed substreams. Record hardware, versions, affinity and load. Prefix totals retain first-use costs; never extrapolate the rebuild baseline or the 2048-cell stress grid to unmeasured query counts.
replay: Save compressed JSONL proofs and query results for every method and query. Replay every proof outside the timed serving path with a fresh checker per trusted view; reuse that checker across its queries. Save interval/source-count/view digests and all numerical failures.
versions: Public highspy 1.15.1 for cold and basis-hot-start comparators; SciPy 1.18.0 bundled HiGHS 1.12.0 for component/global-fallback proposals. Both are pre-existing project dependencies; record actual versions.
stopping_rule: Complete the entire declared grid and all three repeats; no positive-speedup stopping. Stop only for invalid proofs, data mismatch or code exceptions, preserving partial results and recording corrections.
